- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike (≥5% from prior) with negative sentiment, it often overcorrects; cap forecast at 1–2% above prior peak.
- If model underestimates in early period (e.g., first 5–7 days) and sentiment is neutral or slightly negative, adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to align with mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤-0.3) mid-period, model often fails to anticipate downward correction; add 1–2% downward bias to forecast from that point onward.
- Model tends to lag in capturing sentiment shifts — if sentiment changes direction within 3–5 days, adjust forecast 1–3 days ahead to reflect new sentiment trend.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid extreme outliers (e.g., >10% above or below 14-day moving average) unless sentiment strongly supports it; use sentiment as filter for outlier rejection.
